quote: Run fast bonded/nonbonded substeps concurrently with one speculative slow force evaluation using extrapolated positions; commit substeps and roll back only when a rare collision or large-force rejection triggers a resimulation.
reason: Extrapolated-position speculation changes the computation and overlaps fast substeps with the slow force step, removing the timestep barrier.

quote: Use ParaExp/PFASST-style parallel-in-time splitting: a coarse propagator provides initial values so fine timestep chunks integrate concurrently on multiple GPUs, and corrections iterate only where coarse error is large.
reason: Coarse propagator guesses plus corrections change the computation; fine timestep chunks integrate simultaneously, breaking serial time integration.

quote: Peel the de Bruijn graph in parallel across independent components, and speculatively extend multiple branches at each fork; commit the branch with best read-depth and mismatch support, rolling back rejected alternatives.
reason: Speculation changes the computation: fork alternatives extend simultaneously instead of one-edge-at-a-time walking dependent on committed sequence.

quote: Replace label propagation with union-find plus pointer jumping and tree contraction: GPU blocks merge edges in parallel, then resolve parent chains via atomic compare-and-swap until roots stabilize.
reason: Union-find with pointer jumping computes chain resolution simultaneously across particles, removing the step-by-step label propagation cascade.

quote: Use algebraic tensor factorization and persistent kernels to flatten the contraction DAG; distribute occupied and virtual blocks across GPUs and overlap communication with compute to shorten the critical path.
reason: Factorization reorders contractions so GPUs shorten one iteration's critical path, but iterations stay sequential and gains come from intra-step GPU splitting.
